```csharp
using CRM_Morcaffein.Controllers;
using CRM_Morcaffein.api.DTOs;
using CRM_Morcaffein.domain.entities;
using CRM_Morcaffein.Session;
using CRM_Morcaffein.Theme;
using CRM_Morcaffein.winforms.Services;
using CRM_Morcaffein.winforms.Services.Api;

namespace CRM_Morcaffein.winforms.Views.Controls
{
    /// <summary>
    /// The Transactions/POS tab.
    ///
    /// Layout (top to bottom):
    ///   Row 1  — customer search box + Go, profile summary to its right (full width)
    ///   Row 2  — drinks catalog (left, fills) + Order / Payables / Log Sale (right, 380px)
    ///
    /// The catalog is a wrapper-Panel (AutoScroll) hosting a TableLayoutPanel with the
    /// product cards. The wrapper scrolls; the grid is absolutely positioned inside it and
    /// its height is set explicitly per row count — this is the only reliable way to get
    /// AutoScroll to fire on a WinForms grid.
    ///
    /// Customer selection gates the middle+right area via a non-docked overlay panel that
    /// tracks the Row 2 container's bounds.
    /// </summary>
    public class TransactionView : UserControl
    {
        // ---------------------------------------------------------------------
        // Layout constants
        // ---------------------------------------------------------------------
        private const int DrinksColumnCount = 5;
        private const int DrinksRowHeight = 216;
        private const int CustomerAreaHeight = 96;
        private const int RightColumnWidth = 380;
        private const string AllCategoriesOption = "All Categories";
        private const decimal VatRate = 0.12m;

        // ---------------------------------------------------------------------
        // State
        // ---------------------------------------------------------------------
        private TransactionController? _controller;
        private string _selectedCategory = string.Empty;
        private string _lastProductFilterSignature = string.Empty;

        private IReadOnlyList<Product>? _cachedProducts;
        private IReadOnlyList<string>? _cachedCategories;
        private IReadOnlyList<ProductModifier>? _cachedModifiers;

        private System.Windows.Forms.Timer _productSearchDebounce = null!;

        // ---------------------------------------------------------------------
        // Row 1: customer area
        // ---------------------------------------------------------------------
        private TextBox _customerSearchTxtBx = null!;
        private Label _customerSearchErrorLabel = null!;
        private Panel _customerProfilePanel = null!;
        private Label _customerProfileNameLabel = null!;
        private Label _customerProfileDetailLabel = null!;

        // ---------------------------------------------------------------------
        // Row 2, left: drinks
        // ---------------------------------------------------------------------
        private TextBox _productSearchTxtBx = null!;
        private ComboBox _categoryCombo = null!;
        private Panel _productsScrollHost = null!;
        private TableLayoutPanel _productsGrid = null!;

        // ---------------------------------------------------------------------
        // Row 2, right: order / payables / log sale
        // ---------------------------------------------------------------------
        private FlowLayoutPanel _cartLinesPanel = null!;
        private Label _cartEmptyLabel = null!;
        private Label _subTotalValueLabel = null!;
        private Label _discountValueLabel = null!;
        private Label _vatValueLabel = null!;
        private Label _pwdSeniorValueLabel = null!;
        private CheckBox _pwdSeniorChk = null!;
        private Label _totalValueLabel = null!;
        private Label _cartStatusLabel = null!;
        private Button _promoMenuBtn = null!;
        private Button _logSaleBtn = null!;

        // ---------------------------------------------------------------------
        // Overlay (blocks Row 2 until a customer is searched)
        // ---------------------------------------------------------------------
        private Panel _blockOverlayPanel = null!;

        // =====================================================================
        // CONSTRUCTION
        // =====================================================================

        public TransactionView()
        {
            BuildLayout();

            typeof(Control)
                .GetProperty("DoubleBuffered",
                    System.Reflection.BindingFlags.Instance | System.Reflection.BindingFlags.NonPublic)
                ?.SetValue(_productsGrid, true);

            RefreshSummary();
        }

        protected override void Dispose(bool disposing)
        {
            if (disposing)
                _productSearchDebounce?.Dispose();

            base.Dispose(disposing);
        }

        // =====================================================================
        // LAYOUT
        // =====================================================================

        private void BuildLayout()
        {
            Dock = DockStyle.Fill;
            BackColor = BrandPalette.SurfaceSecondary;

            var cardOuterPanel = new Panel
            {
                Dock = DockStyle.Fill,
                BackColor = BrandPalette.SurfaceSecondary,
                Padding = new Padding(24),
            };

            var tableCardPanel = new Panel
            {
                Dock = DockStyle.Fill,
                BackColor = BrandPalette.SurfacePrimary,
            };

            // Row 1 — customer area, full width, docked top.
            var customerArea = BuildCustomerArea();

            // Row 2 — drinks + order/payables, fills the rest.
            var lowerRow = new Panel
            {
                Dock = DockStyle.Fill,
                BackColor = BrandPalette.SurfacePrimary,
            };

            var drinksArea = BuildDrinksArea();
            var rightColumn = BuildOrderColumn();

            lowerRow.Controls.Add(drinksArea);
            lowerRow.Controls.Add(rightColumn);

            // Overlay — absolutely positioned over lowerRow, brought to front. Covers
            // Row 2 only; the customer search box in Row 1 stays usable.
            _blockOverlayPanel = new Panel
            {
                BackColor = BrandPalette.SurfaceCard,
                Visible = true,
            };

            var overlayMessage = new Label
            {
                Text = "Search for a customer to begin.",
                Dock = DockStyle.Fill,
                TextAlign = ContentAlignment.MiddleCenter,
                Font = BrandPalette.BrandFontRegular(12f),
                ForeColor = BrandPalette.NeutralTextMuted,
                BackColor = Color.Transparent,
            };
            _blockOverlayPanel.Controls.Add(overlayMessage);

            lowerRow.Controls.Add(_blockOverlayPanel);
            _blockOverlayPanel.BringToFront();

            void FitOverlay()
            {
                _blockOverlayPanel.Bounds = new Rectangle(
                    0, 0,
                    lowerRow.ClientSize.Width,
                    lowerRow.ClientSize.Height);
            }
            lowerRow.Resize += (s, e) => FitOverlay();
            FitOverlay();

            tableCardPanel.Controls.Add(lowerRow);
            tableCardPanel.Controls.Add(customerArea);

            cardOuterPanel.Controls.Add(tableCardPanel);
            Controls.Add(cardOuterPanel);
        }

        // =====================================================================
        // ROW 1 — CUSTOMER AREA
        // =====================================================================

        private Panel BuildCustomerArea()
        {
            var area = new Panel
            {
                Dock = DockStyle.Top,
                Height = CustomerAreaHeight,
                BackColor = BrandPalette.SurfaceCard,
                Padding = new Padding(12),
            };

            // --- Search row (left) ---
            // Fixed height + absolute-positioned children. Dock.Fill on the textbox made
            // it stretch to the panel's full height while the button drew at its own
            // intrinsic height, so they could never align. Pinning both to the same
            // y/height is the only reliable way.
            const int searchRowHeight = 34;
            const int searchButtonWidth = 80;
            const int searchRowWidth = 360;

            var searchRow = new Panel
            {
                Dock = DockStyle.Left,
                Width = searchRowWidth,
                Height = searchRowHeight,
            };

            _customerSearchTxtBx = new TextBox
            {
                Location = new Point(0, 0),
                Width = searchRowWidth - searchButtonWidth,
                Height = searchRowHeight,
                PlaceholderText = "Customer ID or phone",
                Font = BrandPalette.BrandFontRegular(10.5f),
                BorderStyle = BorderStyle.FixedSingle,
            };

            _customerSearchTxtBx.KeyDown += (s, e) =>
            {
                if (e.KeyCode == Keys.Enter)
                {
                    RunCustomerSearch();
                    e.SuppressKeyPress = true;
                }
            };

            _customerSearchTxtBx.KeyPress += (s, e) =>
            {
                // Numeric only — the POS search accepts Customer ID or phone.
                if (!char.IsControl(e.KeyChar) && !char.IsDigit(e.KeyChar))
                    e.Handled = true;
            };

            var searchBtn = new Button
            {
                Text = "Search",
                Location = new Point(searchRowWidth - searchButtonWidth, 0),
                Width = searchButtonWidth,
                Height = searchRowHeight,
                FlatStyle = FlatStyle.Flat,
                BackColor = BrandPalette.ButtonSecondaryFill,
                ForeColor = BrandPalette.ButtonSecondaryText,
                Font = BrandPalette.BrandFontRegular(9f),
                Cursor = Cursors.Hand,
                Padding = new Padding(0),
                TextAlign = ContentAlignment.MiddleCenter,
            };
            searchBtn.FlatAppearance.BorderSize = 0;
            searchBtn.Click += (s, e) => RunCustomerSearch();

            searchRow.Controls.Add(_customerSearchTxtBx);
            searchRow.Controls.Add(searchBtn);

            // --- Profile (right of search) ---
            // Transparent — no background, no border. Only the content reads as the
            // "highlight": the name is brand brown, the detail line muted.
            _customerProfilePanel = new Panel
            {
                Dock = DockStyle.Left,
                Width = 320,
                Visible = false,
                BackColor = Color.Transparent,
                Padding = new Padding(24, 4, 8, 4),
            };

            _customerProfileNameLabel = new Label
            {
                Dock = DockStyle.Top,
                Height = 26,
                Font = BrandPalette.BrandFontBold(12f),
                ForeColor = BrandPalette.Brand,
                BackColor = Color.Transparent,
            };

            _customerProfileDetailLabel = new Label
            {
                Dock = DockStyle.Top,
                Height = 22,
                Font = BrandPalette.BrandFontRegular(9.5f),
                ForeColor = BrandPalette.NeutralTextMuted,
                BackColor = Color.Transparent,
            };

            _customerProfilePanel.Controls.Add(_customerProfileDetailLabel);
            _customerProfilePanel.Controls.Add(_customerProfileNameLabel);

            // --- Error label (shares the profile slot) ---
            _customerSearchErrorLabel = new Label
            {
                Dock = DockStyle.Fill,
                TextAlign = ContentAlignment.MiddleLeft,
                Padding = new Padding(24, 0, 0, 0),
                Font = BrandPalette.BrandFontRegular(9f),
                ForeColor = BrandPalette.StatusNegativeFill,
                BackColor = Color.Transparent,
            };

            // Add order: Fill-docked error label first, then the Left-docked profile panel
            // and search row. Only one of profile/error is visible at a time, so they never
            // fight for the same space in practice.
            area.Controls.Add(_customerSearchErrorLabel);
            area.Controls.Add(_customerProfilePanel);
            area.Controls.Add(searchRow);

            return area;
        }

        // =====================================================================
        // ROW 2, LEFT — DRINKS
        // =====================================================================

        private Panel BuildDrinksArea()
        {
            var area = new Panel
            {
                Dock = DockStyle.Fill,
                BackColor = BrandPalette.SurfacePrimary,
            };

            var header = new Panel
            {
                Dock = DockStyle.Top,
                Height = 100,
                Padding = new Padding(16, 14, 16, 10),
            };

            // --- Search row ---
            var searchRow = new Panel
            {
                Dock = DockStyle.Top,
                Height = 38,
                Margin = new Padding(0, 0, 0, 12),
                Padding = new Padding(0, 2, 0, 2),
            };

            _productSearchTxtBx = new TextBox
            {
                Dock = DockStyle.Fill,
                PlaceholderText = "Search drinks by name",
                Font = BrandPalette.BrandFontRegular(11f),
                BorderStyle = BorderStyle.FixedSingle,
            };

            // Debounce — only refresh after the user pauses typing. Rebuilding a 40-card
            // TableLayoutPanel on every keystroke was the source of the visible lag.
            _productSearchDebounce = new System.Windows.Forms.Timer { Interval = 200 };
            _productSearchDebounce.Tick += (s, e) =>
            {
                _productSearchDebounce.Stop();
                RefreshProductsPanel();
            };

            _productSearchTxtBx.TextChanged += (s, e) =>
            {
                _productSearchDebounce.Stop();
                _productSearchDebounce.Start();
            };

            searchRow.Controls.Add(_productSearchTxtBx);

            // --- Sort row ---
            var sortRow = new Panel { Dock = DockStyle.Top, Height = 34 };

            var drinksLabel = new Label
            {
                Text = "Drinks",
                AutoSize = true,
                Font = BrandPalette.BrandFontBold(13f),
                ForeColor = BrandPalette.NeutralText,
                BackColor = Color.Transparent,
            };

            var sortLabel = new Label
            {
                Text = "Sort by Category:",
                AutoSize = true,
                Font = BrandPalette.BrandFontRegular(9.5f),
                ForeColor = BrandPalette.NeutralTextMuted,
                BackColor = Color.Transparent,
            };

            _categoryCombo = new ComboBox
            {
                Size = new Size(180, 30),
                DropDownStyle = ComboBoxStyle.DropDownList,
                Font = BrandPalette.BrandFontRegular(9.5f),
            };
            _categoryCombo.SelectedIndexChanged += (s, e) =>
            {
                if (_categoryCombo.SelectedItem is not string category) return;
                _selectedCategory = category == AllCategoriesOption ? string.Empty : category;
                RefreshProductsPanel();
            };

            var drinksWidth = TextRenderer.MeasureText(drinksLabel.Text, drinksLabel.Font).Width;
            var sortLabelWidth = TextRenderer.MeasureText(sortLabel.Text, sortLabel.Font).Width;

            drinksLabel.Left = 0;
            drinksLabel.Top = 0;

            sortLabel.Left = drinksWidth + 24;
            sortLabel.Top = (sortRow.Height - sortLabel.Height) / 2 + 2;

            _categoryCombo.Left = drinksWidth + 24 + sortLabelWidth + 14;
            _categoryCombo.Top = (sortRow.Height - _categoryCombo.Height) / 2;

            sortRow.Controls.Add(drinksLabel);
            sortRow.Controls.Add(sortLabel);
            sortRow.Controls.Add(_categoryCombo);

            var divider = new Panel
            {
                Dock = DockStyle.Bottom,
                Height = 1,
                BackColor = BrandPalette.Border,
            };

            header.Controls.Add(sortRow);
            header.Controls.Add(searchRow);
            header.Controls.Add(divider);

            // --- Scroll host + grid ---
            // The wrapper Panel owns AutoScroll. The grid is ABSOLUTELY positioned inside
            // it (no Dock), and its width/height are set explicitly — a Dock.Top/Fill child
            // of an AutoScroll panel gets its size re-managed by the dock engine, which is
            // why the scrollbar never appeared on the previous attempts.
            _productsScrollHost = new Panel
            {
                Dock = DockStyle.Fill,
                AutoScroll = true,
                BackColor = BrandPalette.SurfacePrimary,
            };

            _productsGrid = new TableLayoutPanel
            {
                Location = new Point(0, 0),
                ColumnCount = DrinksColumnCount,
                RowCount = 0,
                AutoScroll = false,
                Padding = new Padding(12),
                BackColor = BrandPalette.SurfacePrimary,
                GrowStyle = TableLayoutPanelGrowStyle.AddRows,
            };

            for (int i = 0; i < DrinksColumnCount; i++)
                _productsGrid.ColumnStyles.Add(new ColumnStyle(SizeType.Percent, 100f / DrinksColumnCount));

            _productsScrollHost.Controls.Add(_productsGrid);
            _productsScrollHost.Resize += (s, e) => SyncProductsGridWidth();

            area.Controls.Add(_productsScrollHost);
            area.Controls.Add(header);

            return area;
        }

        private void SyncProductsGridWidth()
        {
            if (_productsScrollHost is null || _productsGrid is null)
                return;

            var hostWidth = _productsScrollHost.ClientSize.Width;
            if (hostWidth <= 0)
                return;

            _productsGrid.Width = hostWidth;
        }

        // =====================================================================
        // ROW 2, RIGHT — ORDER / PAYABLES / LOG SALE
        // =====================================================================

        // =====================================================================
        // CATALOG LOADING
        // =====================================================================

        private async Task EnsureCatalogLoadedAsync()
        {
            if (_cachedProducts is not null) return;

            var catalog = await ProductCatalogCache.GetCatalogAsync();

            _cachedProducts = catalog.Products.Select(MapToProductEntity).ToList();
            _cachedCategories = catalog.Categories;
            _cachedModifiers = catalog.Modifiers.Select(MapToModifierEntity).ToList();
        }

        private static Product MapToProductEntity(ProductResponseDto dto)
        {
            var product = new Product
            {
                ProductId = dto.ProductId,
                ProductCode = dto.ProductCode,
                ProductName = dto.ProductName,
                ProductCategory = dto.ProductCategory,
                BasePrice = dto.BasePrice,
                ImageUrl = dto.ImageUrl,
                LocalImagePath = dto.LocalImagePath,
                IsAvailable = dto.IsAvailable,
            };

            foreach (var sizeDto in dto.Sizes)
            {
                product.ProductSizes.Add(new ProductSize
                {
                    ProductSizeId = sizeDto.ProductSizeId,
                    ProductId = dto.ProductId,
                    SizeName = sizeDto.SizeName,
                    Price = sizeDto.Price,
                });
            }

            return product;
        }

        private static ProductModifier MapToModifierEntity(ProductModifierResponseDto dto) => new()
        {
            ProductModifierId = dto.ProductModifierId,
            Name = dto.Name,
            Category = dto.Category,
            Price = dto.Price,
        };

        private static Campaign MapToCampaignEntity(CampaignResponseDto dto) => new()
        {
            CampaignId = dto.CampaignId,
            PromoName = dto.PromoName,
            PromoCategory = dto.PromoCategory,
            DiscountType = dto.DiscountType,
            DiscountValue = dto.DiscountValue,
            TargetTier = dto.TargetTier,
            MinPurchaseAmount = dto.MinPurchaseAmount,
            MaxDiscountAmount = dto.MaxDiscountAmount,
            MaxRedemptionsPerCustomer = dto.MaxRedemptionsPerCustomer,
            StartDate = dto.StartDate,
            EndDate = dto.EndDate,
            IsActive = dto.IsActive,
        };

        // =====================================================================
        // CUSTOMER SELECTION
        // =====================================================================

        private async void RunCustomerSearch()
        {
            var query = _customerSearchTxtBx.Text.Trim();
            if (string.IsNullOrEmpty(query))
                return;

            try
            {
                var customerApi = new CustomerApi();
                var match = await customerApi.FindCustomerAsync(query);

                if (match is null)
                {
                    _customerSearchErrorLabel.Text = $"No customer found for \"{query}\".";
                    _customerProfilePanel.Visible = false;
                    _blockOverlayPanel.Visible = true;
                    return;
                }

                _customerSearchErrorLabel.Text = string.Empty;
                ShowCustomerProfile(match);
                await SelectCustomerAsync(match);
            }
            catch (Exception ex)
            {
                _customerSearchErrorLabel.Text = ex.Message;
                _customerProfilePanel.Visible = false;
                _blockOverlayPanel.Visible = true;
            }
        }

        private void ShowCustomerProfile(CustomerResponseDto customer)
        {
            _customerProfileNameLabel.Text = customer.FullName;
            _customerProfileDetailLabel.Text = $"{customer.Tier} Tier   •   {customer.PointsBalance} pts\n{customer.ContactNumber}";
            _customerProfilePanel.Visible = true;
        }

        private async Task SelectCustomerAsync(CustomerResponseDto dto)
        {
            var employeeId = EmployeeSession.Current?.EmployeeId
                ?? throw new InvalidOperationException("No employee session — the Transaction view requires a logged-in employee.");

            if (_controller is not null && _controller.CartItems.Count > 0)
            {
                var currentCustomerName = _controller.Customer.FullName;
                var confirm = MessageBox.Show(
                    FindForm(),
                    $"Discard the in-progress order for {currentCustomerName} and start a new one for {dto.FullName}?",
                    "Start New Transaction",
                    MessageBoxButtons.YesNo,
                    MessageBoxIcon.Warning);

                if (confirm != DialogResult.Yes)
                {
                    _customerSearchTxtBx.Text = _controller.Customer.CustomerId.ToString();
                    return;
                }
            }

            try
            {
                await EnsureCatalogLoadedAsync();

                var entity = new Customer
                {
                    CustomerId = dto.CustomerId,
                    FirstName = dto.FirstName,
                    LastName = dto.LastName,
                    ContactNumber = dto.ContactNumber,
                    Email = dto.Email,
                    Birthday = dto.Birthday,
                    LastVisitDate = dto.LastVisitDate,
                    PointsBalance = dto.PointsBalance,
                    IsActive = dto.IsActive,
                };

                var campaignDtos = await CampaignCache.GetActiveCampaignsAsync();
                var campaigns = campaignDtos.Select(MapToCampaignEntity).ToList();

                _controller = new TransactionController(
                    _cachedProducts!,
                    _cachedCategories!,
                    _cachedModifiers!,
                    campaigns,
                    entity,
                    employeeId);

                _blockOverlayPanel.Visible = false;

                BuildCategoryOptions();
                RefreshProductsPanel();
                RefreshCartLines();
                RefreshSummary();
            }
            catch (Exception ex)
            {
                _customerSearchErrorLabel.Text = ex.Message;
                _customerProfilePanel.Visible = false;
                _blockOverlayPanel.Visible = true;
            }
        }

        // =====================================================================
        // PROMO
        // =====================================================================

        private void ShowPromoMenu()
        {
            if (_controller is null)
                return;

            var menu = new ContextMenuStrip();

            if (_controller.Order.CampaignRedeems.Count > 0)
            {
                var clear = menu.Items.Add("Clear applied promo");
                clear.Font = BrandPalette.BrandFontBold(9f);
                clear.Click += (s, e) =>
                {
                    _controller.ClearPromos();
                    RefreshSummary();
                    RefreshPromoButton();
                };
                menu.Items.Add(new ToolStripSeparator());
            }

            var eligiblePromos = _controller.GetEligiblePromos();
            if (eligiblePromos.Count == 0)
            {
                var none = menu.Items.Add("No promos available for this order");
                none.Enabled = false;
            }
            else
            {
                foreach (var campaign in eligiblePromos)
                {
                    var alreadyApplied = _controller.Order.CampaignRedeems
                        .Any(r => r.CampaignId == campaign.CampaignId);

                    var label = campaign.DiscountType == "Percentage"
                        ? $"{campaign.PromoName} — {campaign.DiscountValue:0.##}% off"
                        : $"{campaign.PromoName} — ₱{campaign.DiscountValue:0.##} off";
                    if (alreadyApplied)
                        label += "  (applied)";

                    var item = menu.Items.Add(label);
                    item.Enabled = !alreadyApplied;
                    item.Click += (s, e) =>
                    {
                        try
                        {
                            _controller.ApplyPromo(campaign);
                            RefreshSummary();
                            RefreshPromoButton();
                        }
                        catch (Exception ex)
                        {
                            ShowCartStatus(ex.Message);
                        }
                    };
                }
            }

            // Button sits in the Payables box with summary rows above and Log Sale below —
            // open downward so the summary stays visible.
            menu.Show(_promoMenuBtn, new Point(0, _promoMenuBtn.Height));
        }

        private void RefreshPromoButton()
        {
            if (_controller is null)
            {
                _promoMenuBtn.Text = "Select a Promo ▾";
                _promoMenuBtn.Enabled = false;
                return;
            }

            var applied = _controller.Order.CampaignRedeems.FirstOrDefault();

            if (applied is null)
            {
                _promoMenuBtn.Text = "Select a Promo ▾";
            }
            else
            {
                var campaign = _controller.GetEligiblePromos()
                                   .FirstOrDefault(c => c.CampaignId == applied.CampaignId);

                var name = campaign?.PromoName ?? $"Promo #{applied.CampaignId}";
                _promoMenuBtn.Text = $"{name} ▾";
            }

            _promoMenuBtn.Enabled = true;
        }

        private void RefreshSummary()
        {
            RefreshPromoButton();

            if (_controller is null)
            {
                _subTotalValueLabel.Text = "₱0.00";
                _discountValueLabel.Text = "₱0.00";
                _vatValueLabel.Text = "₱0.00";
                _pwdSeniorValueLabel.Text = "₱0.00";
                _totalValueLabel.Text = "₱0.00";
                _logSaleBtn.Enabled = false;
                _pwdSeniorChk.Enabled = false;
                return;
            }

            _pwdSeniorChk.Enabled = true;

            var subTotal = _controller.SubTotal;
            var afterPromo = subTotal - _controller.TotalDiscount;
            var vatAmount = afterPromo > 0
                ? decimal.Round((afterPromo / 1.12m) * VatRate, 2)
                : 0m;

            _subTotalValueLabel.Text = $"₱{subTotal:0.00}";
            _discountValueLabel.Text = $"₱{_controller.TotalDiscount:0.00}";
            _vatValueLabel.Text = $"₱{vatAmount:0.00}";
            _pwdSeniorValueLabel.Text = $"₱{_controller.PwdSeniorDiscountAmount:0.00}";
            _totalValueLabel.Text = $"₱{_controller.TotalAmount:0.00}";
            _logSaleBtn.Enabled = _controller.HasItems;
        }

        // =====================================================================
        // DRINKS GRID
        // =====================================================================

        private void BuildCategoryOptions()
        {
            if (_cachedCategories is null) return;

            _categoryCombo.Items.Clear();
            _categoryCombo.Items.Add(AllCategoriesOption);
            foreach (var category in _cachedCategories)
                _categoryCombo.Items.Add(category);
            _categoryCombo.SelectedIndex = 0;
        }

        [System.Runtime.InteropServices.DllImport("user32.dll")]
        private static extern int SendMessage(IntPtr hWnd, int wMsg, bool wParam, int lParam);

        private const int WM_SETREDRAW = 0x000B;

        private static void SuspendRedraw(Control control)
        {
            SendMessage(control.Handle, WM_SETREDRAW, false, 0);
        }

        private static void ResumeRedraw(Control control)
        {
            SendMessage(control.Handle, WM_SETREDRAW, true, 0);
            control.Refresh();
        }

        private void RefreshProductsPanel()
        {
            var signature = $"{_selectedCategory}|{_productSearchTxtBx.Text}";
            if (signature == _lastProductFilterSignature && _productsGrid.Controls.Count > 0)
                return;

            _lastProductFilterSignature = signature;

            _productsGrid.SuspendLayout();
            SuspendRedraw(_productsGrid);
            try
            {
                _productsGrid.Controls.Clear();
                _productsGrid.RowStyles.Clear();
                _productsGrid.RowCount = 0;

                if (_controller is null)
                {
                    SyncProductsGridWidth();
                    _productsGrid.Height = _productsScrollHost.ClientSize.Height;
                    return;
                }

                var products = _controller.GetProducts(_selectedCategory, _productSearchTxtBx.Text);

                // Fixed-height product rows plus a Percent(100) spacer row at the end. The
                // spacer absorbs leftover vertical space; without it, TableLayoutPanel
                // expands the LAST row to fill the panel, which stretches partial rows.
                var productRows = (products.Count + DrinksColumnCount - 1) / DrinksColumnCount;

                for (int r = 0; r < productRows; r++)
                    _productsGrid.RowStyles.Add(new RowStyle(SizeType.Absolute, DrinksRowHeight));
                _productsGrid.RowStyles.Add(new RowStyle(SizeType.Percent, 100f));

                _productsGrid.RowCount = productRows + 1;

                for (int i = 0; i < products.Count; i++)
                {
                    var product = products[i];
                    var card = new ProductCardControl(product)
                    {
                        Dock = DockStyle.Fill,
                        Margin = new Padding(4),
                    };
                    card.CardClicked += (s, e) => OpenCustomizerForNewItem(product);
                    card.SizeQuickAdded += (s, size) => QuickAddToCart(product, size);

                    var row = i / DrinksColumnCount;
                    var col = i % DrinksColumnCount;
                    _productsGrid.Controls.Add(card, col, row);
                }

                // Explicit grid size — the wrapper's AutoScroll compares this against its
                // own client height and shows a scrollbar when the grid is taller.
                SyncProductsGridWidth();
                var gridHeight = productRows * DrinksRowHeight
                    + _productsGrid.Padding.Top + _productsGrid.Padding.Bottom;
                _productsGrid.Height = Math.Max(gridHeight, _productsScrollHost.ClientSize.Height);
            }
            finally
            {
                ResumeRedraw(_productsGrid);
                _productsGrid.ResumeLayout(performLayout: true);
                _productsScrollHost.PerformLayout();
            }
        }

        // =====================================================================
        // CART
        // =====================================================================

        private void QuickAddToCart(Product product, ProductSize size)
        {
            if (_controller is null)
            {
                ShowCartStatus("Pick a customer on the left first.");
                return;
            }

            try
            {
                _controller.AddItemToCart(product, size, 1, Enumerable.Empty<ProductModifier>());
                RefreshCartLines();
                RefreshSummary();
            }
            catch (Exception ex)
            {
                ShowCartStatus(ex.Message);
            }
        }

        private void OpenCustomizerForNewItem(Product product)
        {
            if (_controller is null)
            {
                ShowCartStatus("Pick a customer on the left first.");
                return;
            }

            using var form = new FrmItemCustomizer(product, _controller.GetModifiers());

            if (form.ShowDialog(FindForm()) == DialogResult.OK)
            {
                try
                {
                    _controller.AddItemToCart(product, form.SelectedSize, form.Quantity, form.SelectedModifiers);
                    RefreshCartLines();
                    RefreshSummary();
                }
                catch (Exception ex)
                {
                    ShowCartStatus(ex.Message);
                }
            }
        }

        private void RefreshCartLines()
        {
            _cartLinesPanel.Controls.Clear();

            if (_controller is null || _controller.CartItems.Count == 0)
            {
                _cartLinesPanel.Controls.Add(_cartEmptyLabel);
                return;
            }

            var lineWidth = Math.Max(200,
                _cartLinesPanel.ClientSize.Width - SystemInformation.VerticalScrollBarWidth - 8);

            foreach (var item in _controller.CartItems)
            {
                var line = new CartLineControl(item) { Width = lineWidth };
                line.QuantityIncreased += (s, e) => ChangeQuantity(item, +1);
                line.QuantityDecreased += (s, e) => ChangeQuantity(item, -1);
                line.RemoveClicked += (s, e) => RemoveFromCart(item);
                _cartLinesPanel.Controls.Add(line);
            }
        }

        private void RemoveFromCart(OrderItem item)
        {
            if (_controller is null) return;

            _controller.RemoveItem(item);
            RefreshCartLines();
            RefreshSummary();
        }

        private void ChangeQuantity(OrderItem item, int delta)
        {
            if (_controller is null || item.Product is null) return;

            var newQuantity = item.Quantity + delta;
            if (newQuantity <= 0)
            {
                RemoveFromCart(item);
                return;
            }

            var size = item.Product.ProductSizes.First(s => s.ProductSizeId == item.ProductSizeId);
            var modifiers = _controller.GetModifiers()
                .Where(m => item.OrderItemModifiers.Any(om => om.ProductModifierId == m.ProductModifierId));

            try
            {
                _controller.UpdateCartItem(item, size, newQuantity, modifiers);
                RefreshCartLines();
                RefreshSummary();
            }
            catch (Exception ex)
            {
                ShowCartStatus(ex.Message);
            }
        }

        private void ShowCartStatus(string message) => _cartStatusLabel.Text = message;

        private async void CompleteSale()
        {
            if (_controller is null) return;

            try
            {
                _logSaleBtn.Enabled = false;
                _cartStatusLabel.Text = "Saving order...";

                await _controller.CompleteSaleAsync();

                MessageBox.Show(FindForm(),
                    $"Sale completed. {_controller.CompletedPointsEarned} points awarded to {_controller.CompletedCustomerName}.",
                    "Sale Complete", MessageBoxButtons.OK, MessageBoxIcon.Information);

                _controller = null;
                _customerProfilePanel.Visible = false;
                _customerSearchErrorLabel.Text = string.Empty;
                _customerSearchTxtBx.Text = string.Empty;
                _cartStatusLabel.Text = string.Empty;
                _blockOverlayPanel.Visible = true;

                _pwdSeniorChk.Checked = false;

                _lastProductFilterSignature = string.Empty;
                RefreshProductsPanel();
                RefreshCartLines();
                RefreshSummary();
            }
            catch (Exception ex)
            {
                ShowCartStatus(ex.Message);
                _logSaleBtn.Enabled = _controller?.HasItems ?? false;
            }
        }
    }
}
```

---

## What changed vs. what you had

**Search box + Go button (Row 1).** Both controls are absolutely positioned at `y = 0`, both `Height = 34`. The textbox is 280px, button is 80px, row total 360px. They now share the same top/bottom edges exactly. Button reads **"Search"**, not 🔍. If you want the whole row wider, change `searchRowWidth` at the top of `BuildCustomerArea` — everything downstream derives from it.

**Profile panel (Row 1, right of search).** `BackColor = Color.Transparent`, no `BorderStyle`, both child labels also `Color.Transparent`. The name is `BrandPalette.Brand` (brand brown) as the visual highlight, the detail line stays muted grey. No box, no seam — it blends into the `SurfaceCard` strip and only the content reads as "this is who you're serving."

**Scrollbar.** This is the part that was wrong before. The `_productsScrollHost` wrapper (`AutoScroll = true`, `Dock.Fill`) hosts `_productsGrid` with **`Location = new Point(0, 0)` and no `Dock`**. Width is set by `SyncProductsGridWidth()` (called from the host's `Resize` and from `RefreshProductsPanel`). Height is set explicitly to `productRows * 216 + padding`, floored at the host's client height so the grid never disappears when empty. Because the grid is absolutely positioned and its height exceeds the host's client height when content overflows, the host's `AutoScroll` now produces a real scrollbar.

**Debounce.** `_productSearchDebounce` (200ms `Timer`). The grid only rebuilds after you stop typing. `_lastProductFilterSignature` short-circuits identical queries.

**No image preload loop.** Deleted. `ProductCardControl.TryLoadImage` already loads and caches per-card.

**`_pwdSeniorChk` reset.** Simplified — direct `Checked = false`. The old `CheckedChanged -= PwdSeniorChk_ProgrammaticReset; Checked = false; CheckedChanged += PwdSeniorChk_ProgrammaticReset;` dance was pointless (it attached the no-op handler, never removed the real one). The real handler checks `if (_controller is null)` and resets itself, so a plain `Checked = false` after setting `_controller = null` is safe and correct.

**Removed.** `PwdSeniorChk_ProgrammaticReset` (unused), `_blockOverlayMessageLabel` field (local now), `_promoMenuBtn` construction in the old customer column, the `middleAndRightContainer` naming (now `lowerRow`), the old `_lastProductFilterSignature` skip on `CompleteSale` (reset explicitly now so the grid rebuilds after a sale).

---

## Apply and test

1. **Save your old `TransactionView.cs` somewhere** before overwriting.
2. Replace the whole file.
3. Rebuild. The only warnings should be the `FrmCreateEmployee.cs` ones you already had (those are pre-existing, not from this file).
4. Run. Check:
   - Search box + Search button aligned top and bottom. ✅ or ❌
   - Profile shows as brand-brown name with no surrounding box. ✅ or ❌
   - Type slowly in the drinks search — should be smooth, not stuttery. ✅ or ❌
   - Clear the search box → all ~40 drinks → **vertical scrollbar appears on the right of the drinks area**. ✅ or ❌

If any of the four still fails, tell me which one and screenshot it. I'll fix that one thing, not re-issue the whole file.

One thing I couldn't verify: whether `ProductCatalogCache.GetCatalogAsync()`, `CampaignCache.GetActiveCampaignsAsync()`, `CustomerApi.FindCustomerAsync()`, and `OrderApi.CompleteOrderAsync()` all have exactly the signatures I've called them with. I copied them from your existing file verbatim, so they should — but if the compiler complains about one of those lines, send me the error and I'll patch the call, not the whole file.

**回答：**

Based on everything in the plan files, here's where you are and what naturally comes next.

## Where you are

- Staff UI: complete, API-backed, layout fixed (search aligns, profile transparent, drinks scroll, typing smooth).
- The Transaction view is now in the final target layout from the low-fi mock.
- Build is clean (only pre-existing `FrmCreateEmployee` nullable warnings).
- No controller changes needed.

## What "proceed" almost certainly means

Your `ai-context-plan (3.0)` file lists the active work order:

> **STEP 1 — Admin UI**
> **STEP 2 — Manager UI**
> **STEP 3 — SMS / Email**
> **STEP 4 — SuperAdmin × Admin (deferred)**

And `ai-context-plan9-15-26.txt` Delta 4 sharpened it further:

> 1. LOGIN (immediate next — see Delta 2). ← **done**
> 2. SERVER-SIDE ROLE ENFORCEMENT. ← **partial** (JWT works, but the API-side `[Authorize(Roles=...)]` coverage is worth auditing)
> 3. MANAGER SIDE …
> 4. ADMIN SIDE …

Since login is done and the WinForms staff surface is stable, **the next workstream is the Manager/Admin surface — starting with Admin** per plan 3.0's explicit ordering ("STEP 1 — Admin UI"). The most common sub-task at the head of that step is **User Management** (CRUD on Employees + Credentials), because that's the prerequisite for a Manager or Admin ever being able to log in and reach the new surfaces.

## But I don't want to guess wrong on a whole new feature

Before I plan anything, four questions — short answers are fine:

1. **Is it Manager UI, Admin UI, or something smaller first?** Plan 3.0 says Admin first. Your recent momentum (login, layout) might suggest you want to do Manager first so a Manager can actually use the approval queue. Which one?
2. **What's the first slice?** For Admin the natural order is:
   - **a)** User Management (Employees + Credentials CRUD) — lets you seed a real Admin/Manager, which every later surface needs.
   - **b)** Review queue (approve/reject Manager point adjustments, customer edits, campaign creations).
   - **c)** Dashboard tab (read-only).
   For Manager it's:
   - **a)** Approve/reject staff point adjustments.
   - **b)** Resolve/dismiss feedback.
   - **c)** Campaign management (create → Admin approval → activate → SMS).
   - **d)** Customer editing with Admin-review queueing.
   - **e)** Dashboard with PDF export.
3. **Where does it live?** Three options, all of which appear in your plans:
   - **Same WinForms app**, new tabs that appear conditionally based on `EmployeeSession.Current.Employee.Role`. Simplest.
   - **A separate WinForms project** for the Admin console (the "Admin console as a separate app" bullet in Delta 4's "deferred/optional"). Cleaner separation, more scaffolding.
   - **A new mode/tab in the existing shell** — sidebar gains "Manager"/"Admin" entries, gated by role. Middle ground.
4. **Does the current `FrmMain` sidebar already have role-gated placeholders for these, or does everything need to be added?** If you can tell me what the sidebar currently renders for a Barista vs a Manager vs an Admin session, I'll know how much of a scaffold exists.

## My read of the most efficient next step

Given the plan files repeatedly emphasize *"Manager requests, Admin approves"* and the approval chain is the whole point of the role system, I'd bet on:

**Admin UI → User Management first**, because:

- It unblocks everything else (you can't test Manager approvals without a real Manager account, and right now the three seeded credentials are the only ones).
- It's self-contained: one tab, one grid, one modal for create/edit, straightforward `[Authorize(Roles="Admin,SuperAdmin")]` on the API endpoints.
- It establishes the pattern for every subsequent Admin/Manager surface (card layout + searchable grid + drawer/modal detail), the same way you did the Staff UI one tab at a time.

But that's a guess. Tell me which of the four questions above matches your intent and I'll write the plan in the same keyword-searchable format as before — file-by-file, method-by-method, before touching any code.

**回答：**

Good context — the two files cover the domain, API, DTOs, services, and the WinForms side comprehensively. I have everything I need to finish the Manage Users feature. Let me flag the **actual gaps** rather than a laundry list, then propose what "finishing" means.

## What's missing (real gaps, in priority order)

**1. `ManageUsersView` has no `Dispose` override — and it hooks `Load` async.**
Not a leak, but worth knowing: `Load += async (s, e) => await ReloadAsync();` fires the search on every re-parenting if `FrmMain` reuses the control. It doesn't (FrmMain builds a fresh `ManageUsersView()` per tab click), so it's fine. No action; just flagging I checked.

**2. `ManageUsersView` — one real bug I can see from the source.**

In `BuildLayout()`, at the very end:

```csharp
// Initial position; also triggered on resize.
newEmployeeBtn.Left = 300;
```

`newEmployeeBtn` was already added to `cardHeaderPanel` earlier and its `Left` is set by the `cardHeaderPanel.Resize` handler. The line `newEmployeeBtn.Left = 300;` at the *end* of `BuildLayout` overrides the resize-computed position on first paint — before the `Resize` event fires to correct it. On a narrow card this puts the button in the middle of the search box; on a wide card it's a visible one-frame flicker. It's the only line in the file whose comment doesn't match its behavior. **This is one of the "tweaks" you're probably referring to.**

**3. `ManageUsersView` — the search re-fires on every keystroke.**

```csharp
searchTxtBx.TextChanged += async (s, e) => await ReloadAsync();
```

Each keystroke hits the API. Same class of problem we fixed in `TransactionView`. Needs the same debounce.

**4. `ManageUsersView` — `_lastSearchSignature` field exists but is never used.**

```csharp
private string _lastSearchSignature = string.Empty;
```

Declared, assigned nowhere, read nowhere. Dead field. Either remove it or (better) use it to short-circuit redundant reloads.

**5. `FrmMain` Admin nav order vs Manager nav order.**
Admin nav is: Dashboard, Approvals, Manage Users. Manager nav is: Dashboard, Campaign, Customers, Feedback. Plan 3.0 says Admin should have "Dashboard tab, read-only" *and* "everything Manager can do" (section 5 — Admin use cases). Right now Admins cannot reach Customers or Feedback at all. Whether that's intentional (Admins only manage users + approve) or a gap (Admins should also have Customer/Feedback read access) depends on your intent. **Confirm before I touch it** — this is a business-rule call, not a bug.

**6. `FrmCreateEmployee.cs` — the CS8625 warnings from your build log.**
Lines 67, 75, 100, 103, 107. Reading the source you pasted:

```csharp
_contactTxtBx = MakeField("Contact number * (10-11 digits)", null, 0, 0, 464);
_emailTxtBx = MakeField("Email (optional)", null, 0, 0, 464);
_usernameTxtBx = MakeField("Username * (min 3 chars)", null, 0, 0, 464);
_passwordTxtBx = MakeField("Password * (min 4 chars)", null, 0, 0, 464);
_confirmTxtBx = MakeField("Confirm password *", null, 0, 0, 464);
```

`MakeField` is declared `MakeField(string _, Panel parent, ...)` — the second parameter is `Panel`, not `Panel?`. Passing `null` triggers CS8625. The `parent` parameter is never actually used inside `MakeField` (it just constructs a `TextBox` and returns it). Same for `FrmEditEmployee.MakeField(Panel parent, int x)` — it *does* use `parent.Controls.Add(txt)`, so it can't be dropped, but its signature should be `Panel parent` with the caller passing a real panel or the parameter should be removed.

**The clean fix for `FrmCreateEmployee`:** drop the unused `Panel parent` parameter from `MakeField` entirely. It's called with `null` five times and never used. That removes all five CS8625 warnings and simplifies the signature. **This is the second "tweak."**

**7. `FrmLogFeedback` does not cancel the async customer search on close.**

```csharp
private async void CustomerSearchTxtBx_TextChanged(object? sender, EventArgs e)
{
    try
    {
        var results = await _controller.SearchCustomersAsync(customerSearchTxtBx.Text);
        customerResultsListBox.DataSource = results;
    }
    ...
}
```

If the user closes the modal mid-search, the continuation sets `customerResultsListBox.DataSource` on a disposed control. It's caught by the empty `catch` so no crash, but the search also fires on every keystroke (no debounce) — same class of problem. Not strictly part of "finish Manage Users" but adjacent. Flag for later, don't fix now unless you want it in scope.

**8. What I don't have and don't need.**

- `FrmMain.Designer.cs` — not needed; the code I have (`BuildNavButtons`) tells me everything about nav.
- `CustomerManagementView.Designer.cs` / `FeedbackManagementView.Designer.cs` — already documented in the designer bundle.
- `PaginationControl` — I have it.
- All the `Api*` classes, DTOs, and the API side — I have them.

## What "finish Manage Users" means, as I'd scope it

Given the code and your "will need some tweaking" framing, the finish line is:

1. **Fix the `newEmployeeBtn.Left = 300;` override** — remove the line so the resize handler owns positioning.
2. **Add a debounce to the search TextBox** — 200ms, same pattern as `TransactionView`.
3. **Drop the unused `Panel parent` parameter from `FrmCreateEmployee.MakeField`** — kills five CS8625 warnings and simplifies five call sites.
4. **Remove the dead `_lastSearchSignature` field** — or use it. I lean toward using it: short-circuit `ReloadAsync` when the search text hasn't changed since the last load. But only worth it if there's a path where `ReloadAsync` gets called redundantly. The debounce already handles that. I'll remove the field.
5. **Verify the pagination flow** — `_page` tracking, `keepPage` semantics, `ResetToFirstPage()` on search change. Reading the code, `ReloadAsync(keepPage: false)` (the default) resets page to 1, and the search handler calls `ReloadAsync()` → resets. Page button handler calls `ReloadAsync(keepPage: true)` → preserves `_page`. **This is correct.** No fix needed; I just want to confirm I read it right before I touch anything in that area.

That's the whole scope. Four small edits, all in `ManageUsersView.cs` and `FrmCreateEmployee.cs`.

## What I am NOT going to touch without your go-ahead

- **`FrmMain` nav items for Admin.** Adding Customers/Feedback to Admin is a product decision. Confirm: should Admin see them, or is "Admin = Dashboard + Approvals + Manage Users" intentional? - **API-side `EmployeesController`** — the code is clean. One thing I noticed but won't change without asking: `CreateEmployee` blocks Admins from creating Admins, but the *SuperAdmin* is supposed to be able to (per the error message "Only the SuperAdmin can create Admin accounts"). The check is `if (requestedRole is "Admin" or "SuperAdmin") return 403` — it rejects **all** callers, including a SuperAdmin. If SuperAdmin is supposed to create Admins from somewhere (the API directly?), that path is currently blocked. If SuperAdmin doesn't exist as a UI-reachable role and Admins genuinely can't create Admins, the check is fine. **Flagging, not fixing** — I don't know the intent.

```csharp
        /// <summary>

        /// three action buttons also live), so entering edit state hides those buttons and

        private Panel BuildEditPanel()

            const int labelHeight = 18;
            const int fieldHeight = 28;
            const int fieldWidth = 308;

            var panel = new Panel
            {
                Location = new Point(14, 176),

                BackColor = BrandPalette.SurfaceCard,

            TextBox MakeRow(string labelText, bool digitsOnly = false)

                {

                    Font = BrandPalette.BrandFontRegular(9f),
                    ForeColor = BrandPalette.NeutralTextMuted,

                var txt = new TextBox

                        if (!char.IsControl(e.KeyChar) && !char.IsDigit(e.KeyChar))

            panel.Controls.Add(editRoleCombo);
            panel.Controls.Add(roleLabel);

        /// <summary>
        /// Switches combinedBox from "view" state to "edit" state:
        ///   - Hides the three action buttons
        ///   - Shows the edit panel, prefilled from the selected employee
        ///   - Grows combinedBox to fit the edit panel
        /// </summary>
        private void EnterEditState()
        {
            if (_selectedEmployee is null) return;

            var emp = _selectedEmployee;

            editFirstNameTxtBx.Text = emp.FirstName;
            editLastNameTxtBx.Text = emp.LastName;
            editContactTxtBx.Text = emp.ContactNumber;
            editEmailTxtBx.Text = emp.Email ?? string.Empty;
            editUsernameTxtBx.Text = emp.Username ?? string.Empty;

            var roleIndex = editRoleCombo.Items.IndexOf(emp.Role);
            editRoleCombo.SelectedIndex = roleIndex >= 0 ? roleIndex : 0;

            editErrorLabel.Text = string.Empty;

            editBtn.Visible = false;
            resetPasswordBtn.Visible = false;
            deactivateBtn.Visible = false;
            editPanel.Visible = true;

            // Grow the box: edit panel top is y=176 inside combinedBox, plus panel height,
            // plus a 14px bottom inset.
            combinedBox.Height = 176 + editPanel.Height + 14;

            _isEditing = true;
        }

        /// <summary>
        /// Reverts combinedBox to "view" state. Called on Cancel and after a successful Save.
        /// </summary>
        private void ExitEditState()
        {
            editPanel.Visible = false;
            editBtn.Visible = true;
            resetPasswordBtn.Visible = true;
            deactivateBtn.Visible = true;

            combinedBox.Height = 340;   // original height
            _isEditing = false;
        }

        private async void EditSaveBtn_Click(object? sender, EventArgs e)
        {
            if (_selectedEmployee is null) return;

            editErrorLabel.Text = string.Empty;

            // Client-side validation — mirrors the server rules.
            if (string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(editFirstNameTxtBx.Text) ||
                string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(editLastNameTxtBx.Text))
            {
                editErrorLabel.Text = "First and last name are required.";
                return;
            }

            var cleanedPhone = new string(editContactTxtBx.Text.Where(char.IsDigit).ToArray());
            if (cleanedPhone.Length < 10 || cleanedPhone.Length > 11)
            {
                editErrorLabel.Text = "Contact number must be 10-11 digits.";
                return;
            }

            if (!string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(editEmailTxtBx.Text) &&
                (!editEmailTxtBx.Text.Contains('@') || !editEmailTxtBx.Text.Contains('.')))
            {
                editErrorLabel.Text = "Invalid email format.";
                return;
            }

            var newUsername = editUsernameTxtBx.Text.Trim();
            if (newUsername.Length < 3)
            {
                editErrorLabel.Text = "Username must be at least 3 characters.";
                return;
            }

            try
            {
                editSaveBtn.Enabled = false;

                await _controller.UpdateAsync(
                    _selectedEmployee.EmployeeId,
                    editFirstNameTxtBx.Text,
                    editLastNameTxtBx.Text,
                    editContactTxtBx.Text,
                    string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(editEmailTxtBx.Text) ? null : editEmailTxtBx.Text,
                    editRoleCombo.SelectedItem as string ?? "Barista",
                    newUsername);

                ExitEditState();
                await ReloadAsync(keepPage: true);
            }
            catch (Exception ex)
            {
                editErrorLabel.Text = ex.Message;
            }
            finally
            {
                editSaveBtn.Enabled = true;
            }
        }

        private static Button MakeActionButton(string text, int y)
```

## Step 2 — Reset Password inline

Same treatment as Edit Information: the modal goes away, the drawer's `combinedBox` swaps to a reset-password state, and Cancel/Save collapses back.

Two things I want to confirm before writing it, since they affect the shape of the patch:

**Q1. Where does the reset-password form live in the box?**

The edit form I just built occupies the slot *below* the divider (where the three action buttons normally sit) and grows the box downward. Reset Password is a 2-field form — much shorter than Edit. Two options:

- **(a)** Same slot as edit. Clicking Reset Password hides the three buttons and shows two password fields + Save/Cancel in their place. Box does **not** need to grow (the two fields + buttons fit in roughly the same vertical space as the three buttons + a little slack — I'd have to check). This matches Edit and keeps the pattern consistent.
- **(b)** Same slot as edit, but the box does grow a bit, because two label+textbox rows + error + buttons is taller than three flat buttons. Which, honestly, is probably the case.

Either way it's the same mechanism I already built — I just need to know whether to force a fixed height or grow-to-fit. My recommendation: **grow-to-fit, same as edit.** Consistent behavior, and the box height math is already written. Unless you'd rather reset password stay compact.

**Q2. Username / contact / etc. — show them while resetting?**

The profile header (name / role / contact / last login / status) stays visible during Edit because you're editing *that* data. For Reset Password, the header still makes sense to show — it tells you *whose* password you're resetting. I'm going to keep it visible unless you say otherwise. Confirm.

**Q3. After a successful reset, does the drawer collapse?**

For Edit, Save collapses back to view and reloads the grid. For Reset Password there's nothing in the grid to reload (the password isn't a grid column). So: collapse to view state, show a small transient confirmation (e.g. the error label goes green and reads "Password reset."), no grid reload. Or just collapse silently. **Which do you prefer?** I lean toward: collapse to view, no message — the fact that the box collapsed is the confirmation. But a brief "Password reset." message is friendlier. Your call.

**Q4. Confirm-password mismatch — check client-side, or rely on the server?**

The API's `ResetPasswordRequest` only takes `NewPassword`. There's no confirmation field server-side; the modal did the mismatch check client-side. I'll keep it client-side in the inline form: if the two textboxes don't match, show the error in the inline `resetErrorLabel` and don't call the API. Same as the old modal. Confirm that's fine, or do you want confirmation to be server-enforced too?

## PATCH A — new file `CRM_Morcaffein/Views/Controls/Toast.cs`

Create the file with this content. Put it in the same folder as the other controls (`Views/Controls/`), namespace `CRM_Morcaffein.winforms.Views.Controls`.

```csharp
using CRM_Morcaffein.Theme;

namespace CRM_Morcaffein.winforms.Views.Controls
{
    /// <summary>
    /// Lightweight, non-blocking confirmation message. A small rounded card that slides
    /// in at the bottom-center of its host, holds for a few seconds, then fades out and
    /// disposes itself. Multiple toasts stack vertically (newest at the bottom).
    ///
    /// Usage:  Toast.Show(this, "Employee created.", ToastKind.Success);
    /// The host can be any Control — typically a UserControl or Form. The toast parents
    /// itself to the host, positions itself, brings itself to front, and cleans up.
    ///
    /// Why a Panel and not a real Form: no title bar, no taskbar entry, no window
    /// activation, no flicker on show. It behaves like a floating child control rather
    /// than a window, which is what we want for transient confirmations.
    /// </summary>
    public enum ToastKind
    {
        Success,
        Info,
        Error,
    }

    public static class Toast
    {
        // Vertical gap between stacked toasts and from the bottom edge of the host.
        private const int BottomMargin = 24;
        private const int ToastGap = 8;
        private const int ToastHeight = 40;
        private const int ToastMinWidth = 260;
        private const int ToastMaxWidth = 460;
        private const int HorizontalPadding = 20;

        // How long the toast stays fully visible before the fade begins.
        private const int HoldMilliseconds = 2400;
        private const int FadeStepMilliseconds = 30;
        private const double FadeStepOpacity = 0.08;

        public static void Show(Control host, string message, ToastKind kind = ToastKind.Success)
        {
            if (host is null || string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(message))
                return;

            // Fonts are shared through BrandPalette; measure the message to size the card.
            var font = BrandPalette.BrandFontRegular(9.5f);
            var textWidth = TextRenderer.MeasureText(message, font).Width;

            var width = Math.Clamp(textWidth + HorizontalPadding * 2, ToastMinWidth, ToastMaxWidth);

            var toast = new Panel
            {
                Width = width,
                Height = ToastHeight,
                BackColor = FillColorFor(kind),
                // No border — the fill color carries the state.
            };

            var label = new Label
            {
                Text = message,
                Dock = DockStyle.Fill,
                TextAlign = ContentAlignment.MiddleCenter,
                Font = font,
                ForeColor = TextColorFor(kind),
                BackColor = Color.Transparent,
                Padding = new Padding(HorizontalPadding, 0, HorizontalPadding, 0),
                AutoEllipsis = true,
            };
            toast.Controls.Add(label);

            host.Controls.Add(toast);
            toast.BringToFront();

            // Position: bottom-center of the host, stacked above any existing toasts.
            void Reposition()
            {
                var hostWidth = host.ClientSize.Width;
                var hostHeight = host.ClientSize.Height;

                var x = Math.Max(0, (hostWidth - toast.Width) / 2);

                // Count toasts already on the host (excluding this one) to compute the stack offset.
                var existing = host.Controls.OfType<Panel>()
                    .Count(c => c != toast && c.Tag is string tag && tag == ToastTag);

                var y = hostHeight - BottomMargin - toast.Height
                        - existing * (ToastHeight + ToastGap);

                toast.Location = new Point(x, y);
            }

            toast.Tag = ToastTag;   // marker so Reposition can find siblings
            Reposition();

            // Recompute position if the host resizes while the toast is alive.
            EventHandler? onResize = null;
            onResize = (s, e) => Reposition();
            host.Resize += onResize;

            // Hold, then fade, then dispose.
            var holdTimer = new System.Windows.Forms.Timer { Interval = HoldMilliseconds };
            holdTimer.Tick += (s, e) =>
            {
                holdTimer.Stop();
                holdTimer.Dispose();

                var fadeTimer = new System.Windows.Forms.Timer { Interval = FadeStepMilliseconds };
                fadeTimer.Tick += (s2, e2) =>
                {
                    // WinForms Panels don't support real per-control opacity without
                    // WS_EX_LAYERED, so "fade" is a color lerp toward the host's background.
                    // The result reads as a smooth dissolve.
                    var target = host.BackColor;
                    var current = toast.BackColor;
                    var next = Lerp(current, target, FadeStepOpacity);

                    if (Math.Abs(next.R - target.R) <= 1 &&
                        Math.Abs(next.G - target.G) <= 1 &&
                        Math.Abs(next.B - target.B) <= 1)
                    {
                        fadeTimer.Stop();
                        fadeTimer.Dispose();
                        host.Resize -= onResize;
                        host.Controls.Remove(toast);
                        toast.Dispose();
                        return;
                    }

                    toast.BackColor = next;
                    label.ForeColor = Lerp(label.ForeColor, target, FadeStepOpacity);
                };
                fadeTimer.Start();
            };
            holdTimer.Start();
        }

        private const string ToastTag = "morcaffein.toast";

        private static Color FillColorFor(ToastKind kind) => kind switch
        {
            ToastKind.Success => BrandPalette.StatusPositiveFill,
            ToastKind.Error => BrandPalette.StatusNegativeFill,
            _ => BrandPalette.SurfaceCard,
        };

        private static Color TextColorFor(ToastKind kind) => kind switch
        {
            ToastKind.Success => BrandPalette.StatusPositiveText,
            ToastKind.Error => BrandPalette.StatusNegativeText,
            _ => BrandPalette.NeutralText,
        };

        private static Color Lerp(Color a, Color b, double amount)
        {
            amount = Math.Clamp(amount, 0.0, 1.0);
            int r = (int)Math.Round(a.R + (b.R - a.R) * amount);
            int g = (int)Math.Round(a.G + (b.G - a.G) * amount);
            int bl = (int)Math.Round(a.B + (b.B - a.B) * amount);
            return Color.FromArgb(255, r, g, bl);
        }
    }
}
```

Two things to know about this:

- **Fade mechanism.** WinForms doesn't do per-control opacity without native tricks, so the "fade" lerps the panel and label colors toward the host's background. On a white card it dissolves cleanly. If you later want a *true* fade, that's a different implementation (layered windows) — flag it if you care.
- **`AutoEllipsis = true` on the label** means very long messages truncate with "…" instead of wrapping. If you'd rather they wrap and the toast grow taller, say so and I'll change it.

```csharp
        {
```

```csharp
            resetErrorLabel.Text = string.Empty;

            var pwd = resetNewPasswordTxtBx.Text;
            var confirm = resetConfirmPasswordTxtBx.Text;

            if (string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(pwd) || pwd.Length < 4)
            {

                return;
            }

            {

            try

                await _controller.ResetPasswordAsync(_selectedEmployee.EmployeeId, pwd);

                ExitToViewState();
                Toast.Show(this, $"Password reset for {_selectedEmployee.FullName}.", ToastKind.Success);
            }
            catch (Exception ex)
            {
                resetErrorLabel.Text = ex.Message;
            }
            finally
            {
                resetSaveBtn.Enabled = true;
            }
```

**提问：**

all works but have comments: -reset password doesnt have the labels anymore, -the toast leaves some kind of panel bug, (next to the pagination buttons) but the toast does show. it also stacks but the problem is it leaves some kind of trail like a footprint like and its not clean

---

**回答：**

Both are my bugs. Let me diagnose from the screenshot before writing fixes.

**Toast footprint.** I can see it in your screenshot — the pale rectangles next to the pagination controls. That's the toast's `Panel` being removed from `host.Controls` **but not from the host's visible surface**, because the *hold* timer runs on a `System.Windows.Forms.Timer` that fires on the UI thread — that part is fine — but the fade-out only recolors the toast toward `host.BackColor`. On the `ManageUsersView`, the host is the UserControl whose own `BackColor` is `SurfaceSecondary` (the light-tan page tint), but the toast sits **on top of the card**, which is `SurfacePrimary` (white). So the lerp drives the toast toward tan, not white — and when the toast finally gets to within 1 RGB of tan, it's still visibly different from the white card underneath. So it "fades" to a slightly-off tint and then... the code does remove and dispose it. But the screenshot shows it lingering.

Wait — re-reading my fade code more carefully. The exit condition is:

```csharp
if (Math.Abs(next.R - target.R) <= 1 &&
    Math.Abs(next.G - target.G) <= 1 &&
    Math.Abs(next.B - target.B) <= 1)
```

The lerp is `current + (target - current) * 0.08` per tick. With `FadeStepOpacity = 0.08`, it approaches the target asymptotically. **It will reach within 1 unit eventually**, but not before a noticeable number of ticks (roughly 60-80 ticks for a big delta). Each tick is 30ms. So the fade takes **2-2.5 seconds** after the 2.4s hold. That's why it looks like a trail.

But that still removes the panel at the end. So the pale rectangles you're seeing are probably **not the toast itself**. They look like two stacked rectangles exactly where toasts would appear — width ~280px, height ~40px each, stacked with a gap. That's the toast geometry.

**My read:** those are actual toast Panels that haven't finished fading yet when you took the screenshot. The screenshot captured the fade mid-flight. Two toasts stacking (a save + something else) look exactly like that while fading.

But you say "it leaves some kind of trail like a footprint like and its not clean." If it never fully disappears, then the removal isn't happening. And I see a real bug in the removal path:

```csharp
host.Resize -= onResize;
host.Controls.Remove(toast);
toast.Dispose();
```

That's fine. But — **the `label` inside the toast is a child of the toast**, so disposing the toast disposes the label. Fine. The `host.Controls.Remove(toast)` is fine. So the toast should go.

**The actual bug I can see:** the fade timer's closure captures `target = host.BackColor` at fade-time. That's `SurfaceSecondary` on the ManageUsersView. The toast's *starting* color is `StatusPositiveFill` (a light tan). Lerping toward `SurfaceSecondary` (another light tan) means the color difference gets small **fast** — so the exit condition `<= 1` on all channels might trigger while the toast still has visible contrast against the **white** card it's sitting on. Then `host.Controls.Remove` runs and it should disappear. Unless...

**Actually, I bet I know what happened.** Look at your screenshot again. The toast rectangles are pale, low-contrast, and positioned bottom-center. And there are two of them, stacked. That's exactly what a fading toast looks like at tick ~10-15. **They may just be caught mid-fade.** Let me not guess — the fix is to make the fade fast, make the end state guaranteed, and remove the "lerp toward host background" heuristic entirely, because it's fragile when host and card backgrounds differ.

**Correct fix for the toast:**

- Don't lerp colors. WinForms can't truly fade a child control. Either (a) hard-cut: hold N seconds, then remove instantly. Or (b) do a **fast** alpha-style fade by swapping through ~6 precomputed colors in ~200ms total, then remove.
- Cleaner option: hold, then one short "shrinking opacity" sequence of 5 steps over 150ms, then remove unconditionally.
- Simplest and most reliable: hold for 2.5s, then **remove instantly**. No fade. Users still see it clearly. If you want a fade, do it in 150ms, not 2.5s.

My recommendation: **hard cut after hold**. No fade. It's clean, it's instant, no trails, no host-background assumptions.

**Reset password labels missing.** Look at `BuildResetPanel`. The `MakeLabel` helper captures `y` at the time it's called, but look at the flow:

```csharp
TextBox MakePwdBox()
{
    var txt = new TextBox
    {
        Location = new Point(0, y + labelHeight),
        ...
    };
    panel.Controls.Add(txt);
    y += rowHeight;
    return txt;
}

var newLabel = MakeLabel("New password * (min 4 chars)");
resetNewPasswordTxtBx = MakePwdBox();

var confirmLabel = MakeLabel("Confirm new password *");
resetConfirmPasswordTxtBx = MakePwdBox();
```

`MakeLabel` puts its label at the *current* `y`. Then `MakePwdBox` puts its textbox at `y + labelHeight` and *then* increments `y`. So:

- `MakeLabel` at y=0 → label at y=0. Good.
- `MakePwdBox` → textbox at y=18, then y=56.
- `MakeLabel` at y=56 → confirm label at y=56. Good.
- `MakePwdBox` → textbox at y=74, then y=112.

That looks right. But the labels are never added to `panel.Controls`! Look:

```csharp
Label MakeLabel(string text) => new()
{
    Text = text,
    ...
};
```

It **constructs and returns** a label, but nothing adds it. `MakePwdBox` does `panel.Controls.Add(txt)`, but `MakeLabel` has no equivalent — the label is orphaned. That's why they're missing.

Fix: make `MakeLabel` add itself, like `MakePwdBox` does. Or add `panel.Controls.Add(newLabel)` after each call.

Also the error label and buttons work, so the fields exist — they just have no labels above them.

If you want a fade later, the correct approach is a short 150ms color animation toward a **hardcoded** target color — not the host background. I'd only add it if you specifically want it; the hard cut is cleaner.

### PATCH 2 — `ManageUsersView.cs` — fix `BuildResetPanel`'s missing labels

**Search for** (inside `BuildResetPanel`):

```csharp
            Label MakeLabel(string text) => new()
            {
                Text = text,
```

**Replace with:**

```csharp
            // Both helpers add their control to the panel — a local function that only
            // *constructs* a Label and returns it would orphan the label with no parent,
            // which is why they weren't rendering.
            void AddLabel(string text, int yPos)
            {
                var label = new Label
                {
                    Text = text,
                    Location = new Point(0, yPos),
                    AutoSize = true,
                    Font = BrandPalette.BrandFontRegular(9f),
                    ForeColor = BrandPalette.NeutralTextMuted,
                };
                panel.Controls.Add(label);
```

Note: `AddLabel` now takes the y explicitly, so it's obvious where each label lands. `MakePwdBox` still reads the current `y` — the label is placed at the pre-increment position, the textbox at `y + labelHeight`, and the counter advances after.
